## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [JIRA](http://www.atlassian.com/software/jira) a J2EE-based, issue tracking and project management application.

## Issue Tracking

Issues, bugs, and feature requests should be submitted to the following issue tracking system for this project.

```
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/DIRECTMEMORY
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-msgpack/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-msgpack/ directmemory-msgpack
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-msgpack/ directmemory-msgpack
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-msgpack/ directmemory-msgpack
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. ## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

#### public [Pointer](../../../../org/apache/directmemory/memory/Pointer.html)<V> allocate (K key, [Class](http://download.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/index.html?java/lang/Class.html)<T> type, int size)

Explicitly allocated a bunch of bytes in the cache using a given key and type and returns the created
`Pointer`.

##### Parameters

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| key The key to store as | |
| type The datatype of the underlying data | |
| size The size to allocate for this pointer | |

#### public void clear ()

Clears the whole cache by removing all stored keys. It is up to the underlying `MemoryManagerService`
implementation to free allocated memory or not.

#### public void close ()

##### Throws

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [IOException](http://download.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/index.html?java/io/IOException.html)  | |

#### public void collectAll ()

Tells the `CacheService` to collect and remove all expired AND least frequently used keys. In most cases
this is automatically handled by scheduling a disposal interval using `scheduleDisposalEvery(long)`
and there are very rare cases where this needs to be called manually.

#### public void collectExpired ()

Tells the `CacheService` to collect and remove all expired keys. In most cases this is automatically
handled by scheduling a disposal interval using `scheduleDisposalEvery(long)` and there are very
rare cases where this needs to be called manually.

#### public void collectLFU ()

Tells the `CacheService` to collect and remove all least frequently used keys. This operation could
possibly clear the whole cache if there were no recent actions. In most cases this is automatically handled by
scheduling a disposal interval using `scheduleDisposalEvery(long)` and there are very rare cases
where this needs to be called manually.

#### public void dump ()

Dumps information about the actual internal `MemoryManagerService` to the configured Logger with
info loglevel.

Retrieves a map of all available keys and their according `Pointer`s. It is up to the `CacheService`
implementation if the retrieved map is threadsafe or not. The standard implementation uses a
ConcurrentHashMap.

# RoundRobinAllocationPolicy

extends [Object](http://download.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/index.html?java/lang/Object.html)  
implements
[AllocationPolicy](../../../../org/apache/directmemory/memory/AllocationPolicy.html)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [java.lang.Object](http://download.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/index.html?java/lang/Object.html) | |
| ↳ | org.apache.directmemory.memory.RoundRobinAllocationPolicy |

## Class Overview

Round Robin allocation policy. An internal counter is incremented (modulo the size of the buffer), so each calls to
#getActiveBuffer(OffHeapMemoryBuffer, int) will increment the counter and return the buffer at the index of
the counter.

| Known Indirect Subclasses [RoundRobinAllocationPolicy](../../../../org/apache/directmemory/memory/RoundRobinAllocationPolicy.html)  |  |  | | --- | --- | | [RoundRobinAllocationPolicy](../../../../org/apache/directmemory/memory/RoundRobinAllocationPolicy.html) | Round Robin allocation policy. | | | | | | | | | | | | |

## Class Overview

Interface describing the buffer allocation policy.
The implementations will be initialized by setting the list of buffers `init(List)`,
and every allocation will call #getActiveBuffer(OffHeapMemoryBuffer, int),
passing the previously (possibly null) buffer that failed to allocate and the number of the current allocation

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [JIRA](http://www.atlassian.com/software/jira) a J2EE-based, issue tracking and project management application.

## Issue Tracking

Issues, bugs, and feature requests should be submitted to the following issue tracking system for this project.

```
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/DIRECTMEMORY
```

---
## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. ## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. ## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-client/ directmemory-server-client
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-msgpack/ directmemory-msgpack
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-ehcache/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-ehcache/ directmemory-ehcache
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-ehcache/ directmemory-ehcache
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-ehcache/ directmemory-ehcache
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-kryo/ directmemory-kryo
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-tests/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-tests/ directmemory-tests
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-tests/ directmemory-tests
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-tests/ directmemory-tests
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. ## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/osgi/ osgi
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/server-example-archetype/ server-example-archetype
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/platforms/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/ platforms
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/ platforms
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/ platforms
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-commons/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-commons/ directmemory-server-commons
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-commons/ directmemory-server-commons
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server-commons/ directmemory-server-commons
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/ directmemory-integrations
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/ directmemory-integrations
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/ directmemory-integrations
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/server-example/ server-example
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-guava/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-guava/ directmemory-guava
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-guava/ directmemory-guava
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-guava/ directmemory-guava
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/itests/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/ itests
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/ itests
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/itests/ itests
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. ## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-solr/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-solr/ directmemory-solr
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-solr/ directmemory-solr
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-integrations/directmemory-solr/ directmemory-solr
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protobuf/ directmemory-protobuf
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/directmemory-server/ directmemory-server
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/examples/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/ examples
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/ examples
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/examples/ examples
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-serializers/directmemory-protostuff/ directmemory-protostuff
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-cache/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-cache/ directmemory-cache
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-cache/ directmemory-cache
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-cache/ directmemory-cache
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/server/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/ server
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/ server
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/server/ server
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-common/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-common/ directmemory-common
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-common/ directmemory-common
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/directmemory-common/ directmemory-common
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

## The Team

A successful project requires many people to play many roles. Some members write code or documentation, while others are valuable as testers, submitting patches and suggestions.

The team is comprised of Members and Contributors. Members have direct access to the source of a project and actively evolve the code-base. Contributors improve the project through submission of patches and suggestions to the Members. The number of Contributors to the project is unbounded. Get involved today. All contributions to the project are greatly appreciated.

## Overview

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at <http://svnbook.red-bean.com/>.

## Web Access

The following is a link to the online source repository.

```
https://svn.apache.org/viewvc/directmemory/trunk/platforms/apache-directmemory/
```

## Anonymous access

The source can be checked out anonymously from SVN with this command:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/apache-directmemory/ apache-directmemory
```

## Developer access

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but Committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/apache-directmemory/ apache-directmemory
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password)

```
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## Access from behind a firewall

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/directmemory/trunk/platforms/apache-directmemory/ apache-directmemory
```

## Access through a proxy

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

This project uses [Jenkins](http://jenkins-ci.org/).

```
https://builds.apache.org/job/directmemory-trunk/
```

No notifiers are defined. Please check back at a later date.

## Dependency Information

### Apache Maven

```
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.apache.directmemory.karaf</groupId>
  <artifactId>apache-directmemory</artifactId>
  <version>0.3-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <type>pom</type>
</dependency>
```

### Apache Buildr

```
'org.apache.directmemory.karaf:apache-directmemory:pom:0.3-SNAPSHOT'
```

### Apache Ant

```
<dependency org="org.apache.directmemory.karaf" name="apache-directmemory" rev="0.3-SNAPSHOT">
  <artifact name="apache-directmemory" type="pom" />
</dependency>
```

### Groovy Grape

```
@Grapes(
@Grab(group='org.apache.directmemory.karaf', module='apache-directmemory', version='0.3-SNAPSHOT')
)
```

### Grails

```
compile 'org.apache.directmemory.karaf:apache-directmemory:0.3-SNAPSHOT'
```

### Leiningen

```
[org.apache.directmemory.karaf/apache-directmemory "0.3-SNAPSHOT"]
```

### SBT

```
libraryDependencies += "org.apache.directmemory.karaf" %% "apache-directmemory" % "0.3-SNAPSHOT"
```
